title: ai-badger project manifest
description: Provenance record written by scaffold.py: exactly what the framework placed into the target repo, so feed-badger can diff project vs framework.

frameworkCommit.description: Framework git HEAD at scaffold time; null when scaffolded from a plugin cache, which has no .git. The version resolves to the commit in that case (ADR-0001 decision 2).

frameworkDirty.description: True when scaffolded from a working tree with uncommitted changes: provenance that is not reproducible. False from a plugin cache, where local edits are impossible.

frameworkRoot.description: Where the framework was when this scaffold was written — the pointer a copied file otherwise lacks (ADR-0007). Relative to the project when the framework is inside it (a self-hosted repo records '.'), absolute otherwise. A machine-local hint, always re-validated against the root predicate before use, so a value from another machine is ignored rather than trusted.

generatedAt.description: ISO timestamp stamped by the orchestrator after scaffold (scripts avoid nondeterministic clocks).

skillScope.description: Renamed from pluginScope in v0.7.0. scaffold.py still writes both keys so pre-0.7.0 manifests stay readable; pluginScope is deprecated and read by nothing.

configHash.description: sha256 of the config.json this scaffold was built from, canonicalized and minus $schema/frameworkVersion. Absent on manifests written before 0.46.0: refresh re-scaffolds once to record it.

generatedConfig.description: Config files a scaffold run generated or merged into but does not own — `.mcp.json`, `.github/mcp.json`, `.claude/settings.json` (issue #194). Bookkeeping, not ownership: nothing reads a record back to overwrite, delete or drift-check the file, so a path listed here is still the project's to edit. A record outlives the run that wrote it while the file is on disk, and dies with the file; it says only "ai-badger wrote here, at this version". Absent on manifests written before 0.52.0, where authorship could only be inferred from key shape (mcp_tools.only_generated_entries).

path.description: Path within the target repo, recorded whether or not the file is tracked: the record is of writes, not of version control.

destination.description: The label ai-badger knows the destination by — `mcp_tools.McpDestination.label` for the MCP configs, the file's own path for the rest. A destination whose label is not a project path is proposal-only (ADR-0014 decision 6) and is never recorded, because nothing is written.

frameworkVersion.description: The version that last wrote this path; carried forward unchanged from an earlier run's record when this run did not write the file.

hash.description: sha256 of the source content at scaffold time. For directory entries this covers the written target, so it answers whether the project edited its own copy — see sourceHash for framework drift.

seedOnce.description: True where the scaffolder seeds this target once and never rewrites it (.ai-badger/state.json, .ai-badger/agent-instructions/model.json, any scaffolding.json entry marked seedOnce), so the project owns it thereafter. Every other entry is rewritten on the next run, which is what generated_file_guard.py refuses an edit to. Absent on manifests written before 0.101.0: the guard reads absence as regenerated and refuses, because a wrong refusal is loud, overridable and healed by one re-scaffold, while a wrong exemption is the silent loss this guard exists to prevent.

projectOwned.description: Skill directory entries only: the paths inside this delivered skill that the scaffolder stashes and restores across a re-scaffold rather than rewriting — `project-local.md` plus that skill's SEED_ONCE_SKILL_FILES. A skill is one entry for a whole directory, so without this list generated_file_guard.py cannot tell a copied file from a preserved one, and refuses the edit scaffold_freshness_guard.py accepts. Written from the same list the preservation reads, so a newly preserved name needs no second edit. Absent on manifests written before 0.107.0: the guard reads absence as regenerated and refuses, for the reason seedOnce gives.

sourceHash.description: Directory entries only: sha256 of the framework source directory at scaffold time. The only hash that can answer whether the framework has moved ahead, because the target is rendered output (#110).

dirMeta.description: Directory entries only: structural fingerprint drift.py compares before the content hash.

sourceMeta.description: Directory entries only: the same structural pre-check for the framework source directory.
